items.title: Real-Time Vision-Language Model Guided Semantic-Aware Diffusion Navigation with Intelligent Vehicle Validation
items.topic: Real-Time Vision-Language Model Guided Semantic-Aware Diffusion Navigation with Intelligent Vehicle Validation
items.source: 2025 IEEE 28th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC)
items.summary: The 2025 IEEE 28th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC) presents a vision-language model guided semantic-aware diffusion navigation method (VLSAN) for semi-structured campus road scenarios. VLSAN translates natural language instructions into vehicle motion control by leveraging a vision-language model (VLM) to generate semantically guided drivable region maps, achieving multimodal information fusion and semantic alignment.

items.title: Adaptive stress testing of autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions: A large language model (LLM) distillation approach
items.topic: Adaptive stress testing of autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions: A large language model (LLM) distillation approach
items.source: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
items.summary: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies (2027) introduces an adaptive stress testing approach for autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions using a large language model (LLM) distillation method. The approach aims to enhance the robustness and safety of AVs by simulating and testing interactions under various stress conditions, ensuring reliable performance in real-world scenarios.

items.title: What If I Cannot Always See: Misdetection-Aware MPC for Autonomous Vehicles
items.topic: What If I Cannot Always See: Misdetection-Aware MPC for Autonomous Vehicles
items.source: IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems
items.summary: IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems (2026) investigates misdetection-aware model predictive control (MPC) for autonomous vehicles. The paper identifies a critical detection-rate threshold below which collision risk increases sharply, particularly for conventional controllers. This research highlights the importance of addressing intermittent perception errors to ensure AV safety.
